name: Streymin Bridge
facts: The Streymin Bridge opened on 30 October 1973, linking Streymoy to Eysturoy's western half before the 1976 Norðskálatunnilin gave it full inter-regional status.
Dredged to 4 metres deep, the Sundini sound beneath the Streymin Bridge now accommodates ships with a 17‑metre clearance, earning it the nickname “Bridge over the Atlantic.”
After the 2020 Eysturoyartunnilin opened, daily traffic on the Streymin Bridge fell from 4,497 to roughly 2,070 vehicles, yet it remains a core route for Tórshavn‑Klaksvík travelers avoiding tolls.
